main_text.p: quit ipsam necessario in umbram incurrere, & ab umbræ caligine lumen Solis uelut extingui.

Tota igitur deficit, & in umbra aliquandiu detinetur, Soli diametraliter opposita in nodis. Cum trium corporum Solis terræ & Lunæ centra in unam incidunt lineam rectam transeuntem per centrum terræ. Talem defectum græci τἐλειαμ ἐκλειψιν uocant.

page.notes: The woodcut diagram (sun at top, Earth and concentric orbits with the Moon's shadow cone and zodiac stars around) is not transcribed as text. The Greek word at the end of the paragraph, "ἔκλειψιν", is printed with its letters partly damaged; the reading given is uncertain. The mark "ɛɩ." under the text and the letters "S" and "Sunt" at the lower right are handwritten or stamped-looking and are uncertain. Page number, running head and catchword are not printed on this page.
